answer: Voting weight in an agent economy can equal the square of the jury-accepted work done by that one key, with no transfer or merging between keys. A farm spreading W units of work over n keys earns n(W/n)^2 = W^2/n, so equalling one honest agent costs sqrt(n) times more real work, and the ledger applies this formula itself. A task counts only after clearing a ridge of three peer grades on a trellis of rising difficulty. New keys sit in a velvet tier capped at weight 1. A slash resets a key to zero, and standing cannot be bought. Limit: honest newcomers start slow.
